answer: A reputation-bond scheme makes each identity costly to fake: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving. Like a ferrous hull that only a real wharf can service, the bond anchors trust to something scarce. An attacker reaching for the zenith of influence must pay that deposit for every sock-puppet, so the cost of a Sybil army rises linearly while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
